name: Morocco
summary: A red field with a green interlaced pentagram, the Seal of Solomon. Red has been the colour of Moroccan banners since the 17th century; the green star was added by Sultan Yusef in 1915.
origin: Red flags were used by Moroccan rulers from the 17th century; red is associated with the Alaouite dynasty, which claims descent from the Prophet Muhammad through his daughter Fatimah.

Because plain red flags were common at sea and easily confused with others, Sultan Yusef added a green pentagram on 17 November 1915, during the French protectorate. The flag remained in use after independence in 1956.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The Alaouite dynasty; also bravery and strength.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Islam; green is associated with the Prophet.

symbols.name: Seal of Solomon
symbols.description: A green five-pointed star drawn as interlaced lines (a pentagram).
symbols.meaning: The link between God and the nation; its five points are commonly linked to the Five Pillars of Islam.

history.label: Plain red flags of the Alaouite sultans

facts: The pentagram is called the Seal of Solomon (Khatam Sulayman) in Morocco; elsewhere the name is often used for the six-pointed star.
Article 4 of the 2011 Constitution defines the flag.
Vietnam's flag is also a single star on red, but yellow and solid.
clues: A green interlaced star on a red field.
Its star was added in 1915 because plain red flags were confused at sea.
Its star is known by the name of a biblical king.
Its red is linked to a royal dynasty.
